definitions.explanation: Personal preferences about what one likes and dislikes, especially regarding food. Often used when talking about being a picky eater or having strong personal preferences.

examples.japanese: {好|す}き{嫌|きら}いはよくない。
examples.english: Being a picky eater is not good.

examples.japanese: うちの{子|こ}は{食|た}べ{物|もの}の{好|す}き{嫌|きら}いが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: My child is very picky about food.

examples.japanese: {好|す}き{嫌|きら}いなく{何|なん}でも{食|た}べられる{人|ひと}がうらやましい。
examples.english: I envy people who can eat anything without being picky.

notes:
Combines {好|す}き (like) and {嫌|きら}い (dislike) into a single compound noun.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {好|す}き{嫌|きら}いが{多|おお}い: to be picky (about food)
- {好|す}き{嫌|きら}いが{激|はげ}しい: to have strong likes and dislikes
- {好|す}き{嫌|きら}いなく: without being picky
- {好|す}き{嫌|きら}いが{少|すく}ない: to not be picky
- {食|た}べ{物|もの}の{好|す}き{嫌|きら}い: food preferences

USAGE:
Most commonly used about food pickiness, especially with children. Can also refer to preferences about people, though this usage is less common. The pattern {好|す}き{嫌|きら}いなく (without likes or dislikes) is frequently used as an adverbial phrase meaning "without being picky."
